basis: Preferred: construct head of a bare relative clause ('ראשׁית [that] בָּרָ֣א …'); the same pointed form is tagged construct elsewhere in OSHB, so the form does not decide the state. Alternative: OSHB's absolute state, an independent clause. Counter-evidence: the noun carries a disjunctive accent, so the Masoretic reading separates it from the verb (absolute). Holmstedt 2002, pp. 123–125: bare restrictive relative, "In the particular beginning [that] God created the heavens and the earth, — v. 2 parenthesis — God said" (ex. 189); listed in his bare-relative database, p. 107 n. 70. Clause-level consequence of the preferred reading: v. 1 is a subordinate time phrase, v. 2 (three verbless/qatal clauses) is parenthetical, and the main clause is v. 3 וַיֹּאמֶר. Not marked in the stream (token-level only). Same construct reading in Rashi (gerund "in the beginning of God's creating", cited by Holmstedt p. 123 n. 91); parallel string Hos 1:2 תְּחִלַּת דִּבֶּר־יְהוָה (construct + finite verb, tagged construct by OSHB). The alternative (absolute "In the beginning God created") is the Masoretic accentuation (tipcha on בְּרֵאשִׁ֖ית), the Septuagint (Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν) and the reading John 1:1 alludes to. Both syntactic databases (ETCBC BHSA 2021; UD Ancient Hebrew PTNK, which builds on MACULA) parse v. 1 as a main clause with בָּרָא as root, i.e. the alternative reading; the preferred reading rests on Holmstedt and the form evidence.
